questions.stem: The Constitution of India has been amended through three different procedures depending on the subject matter. Which article lays down this amendment procedure?
questions.explanation: Article 368 lays down the amendment procedure. THREE methods: (1) SIMPLE MAJORITY of Parliament — for matters like creation of new states (Art 4), admission of states (Art 3), abolition of LC (Art 169), 5th & 6th Schedules — technically outside Art 368; (2) SPECIAL MAJORITY under Art 368(2) — 2/3 of members present & voting + majority of total membership of each House. Used for most amendments. (3) SPECIAL MAJORITY + RATIFICATION BY 1/2 OF STATE LEGISLATURES — for matters affecting the federal structure: election of President (Art 54, 55), executive power of Union/States (73, 162), SC/HC (Parts V-VII), distribution of legislative powers, 7th Schedule, representation in Parliament.

questions.stem: Which is the FIRST Constitutional Amendment of India (1951), and what did it primarily do?

options.option_text: Added the 9th Schedule + restrictions on Article 19 freedoms
Abolished right to property as a Fundamental Right

questions.explanation: The FIRST Amendment (18 June 1951) — passed by the PROVISIONAL Parliament before the first general elections — did three major things: (1) Added the NINTH SCHEDULE (laws immune from judicial review — originally for land reforms like zamindari abolition, after SC struck some down in Champakam Dorairajan 1951). (2) Added 'REASONABLE RESTRICTIONS' under Article 19(2) — public order, friendly foreign relations, incitement to offence. (3) Amended Article 15 to allow special provisions for socially and educationally backward classes (SEBCs). Proposed by Nehru — the FIRST-EVER amendment to the Constitution. Also: provided safeguards for State-run trading against Article 19(1)(g). 9th Schedule immunity was later qualified by IR Coelho (2007) to basic-structure review.

questions.stem: Which Constitutional Amendment is called the 'MINI-CONSTITUTION' due to the sweeping changes it brought during the Emergency?
questions.explanation: 42nd Amendment (1976), passed during the Emergency under Indira Gandhi, was called the MINI-CONSTITUTION for its extensive changes: (1) Added SECULAR, SOCIALIST, INTEGRITY to the Preamble; (2) Added FUNDAMENTAL DUTIES (Part IV-A, Article 51-A — 10 duties, later 11); (3) DPSP given PRIMACY over FRs in certain cases; (4) JUDICIAL REVIEW restricted; (5) Terms of LS/SLA extended from 5 to 6 years (later reversed by 44th); (6) President bound by Cabinet advice (Art 74) — this remained; (7) Administrative tribunals via Art 323A/B added; (8) Education, Forests, Weights & Measures, Protection of Wild Animals moved from State to Concurrent List. Swaran Singh Committee recommendations. Many provisions were reversed by the 43rd and 44th Amendments (Janata govt 1977-79).

questions.stem: Which Constitutional Amendment implemented GST (Goods and Services Tax) in India, effective 1 July 2017?
questions.explanation: 101st Amendment (2016, effective 1 July 2017) — implemented GST. Key changes: (a) Added Article 246A — concurrent power to Union and States on GST; (b) Added Article 269A — distribution of IGST between Union & States; (c) Added Article 279A — GST COUNCIL (FM + State FMs; 2/3 votes by States + 1/3 by Centre, total 3/4 for decisions). Excluded from GST: alcoholic liquor for human consumption, 5 petroleum products (until notified by Council). Subsumed: Central Excise, Service Tax, VAT, Octroi, Luxury Tax, Entry Tax, etc. Four-slab structure: 5/12/18/28% + cess on sin/luxury goods. 99th (2014) = NJAC (struck down by SC 2015); 103rd (2019) = 10% EWS reservation; 105th (2021) = restored state power to identify OBCs.

questions.stem: Which amendment lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 years?
questions.explanation: 61st Amendment (1989, effective March 1989): amended Article 326 to lower the voting age for Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections from 21 to 18 years. Proposed by Rajiv Gandhi govt to enfranchise ~5 crore young voters. First general election with 18+ age: 1989. Previously 21 since 1950. Globally, most democracies now use 18 too. Fun fact: until the amendment, young adults could marry (even earlier, per pre-1978 laws) but couldn't vote.

questions.stem: The 73rd and 74th Amendments (1992) created a THIRD TIER of governance. Which local bodies do they govern, respectively?
questions.explanation: 73rd AMENDMENT (1992, effective 24 April 1993 — celebrated as NATIONAL PANCHAYATI RAJ DAY): added Part IX + Articles 243-243-O + 11th SCHEDULE (29 subjects devolved to Panchayats). Three-tier panchayat: GRAM, MANDAL/BLOCK/PANCHAYAT SAMITI (intermediate), ZILA PARISHAD (district). Reservations: 1/3 seats for women (many states now 50%), proportional for SC/ST. 5-year term. State Election Commission + State Finance Commission (every 5 years). 74th AMENDMENT (1992, effective 1 June 1993): added Part IX-A + Articles 243-P to 243-ZG + 12th SCHEDULE (18 subjects). Three types of urban bodies: NAGAR PANCHAYAT, MUNICIPAL COUNCIL, MUNICIPAL CORPORATION. Both amendments largely based on Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) + Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) + L.M. Singhvi Committee (1986) recommendations.

questions.stem: The 103rd Amendment (2019) provided 10% reservation for which category?

options.option_text: Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) among the unreserved category

questions.explanation: 103rd AMENDMENT (January 2019): inserted Article 15(6) + 16(6), providing 10% reservation in EDUCATION and GOVT EMPLOYMENT to ECONOMICALLY WEAKER SECTIONS (EWS) of citizens NOT covered by SC/ST/OBC reservations (i.e., poor among 'general' category). EWS eligibility: family income < ₹8 lakh/year; does not own >5 acres agri land, >1000 sq ft flat etc. Upheld by SC in Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (November 2022, 3:2 majority). India's total reservation thus exceeds 50% Indra Sawhney (1992) cap, but SC said 50% cap doesn't apply to EWS. 93rd (2005) = Article 15(5) OBC reservation in private educational institutions. 104th (2020) = removed Anglo-Indian nomination from LS + State Assemblies; extended SC/ST reservation till 2030.

questions.stem: Which amendment added the word 'SECULAR' to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: 42nd Amendment (1976) added THREE words to the Preamble: SOCIALIST, SECULAR, and INTEGRITY (in 'sovereignty, unity and INTEGRITY of the Nation'). The original 1950 Preamble described India as a 'SOVEREIGN DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC'; after 42nd, 'SOVEREIGN SOCIALIST SECULAR DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC'. 'SECULAR' is debated — India follows 'principled distance' from religion (not strict French laïcité separation). SR Bommai v. Union of India (1994) declared secularism part of the BASIC STRUCTURE. 44th Amendment (1978) could not undo these additions — they remain. Constituent Assembly had deliberately NOT included 'secular' and 'socialist' originally; they felt it was implicit.

questions.stem: The 44th Amendment (1978) made three key reversals of the 42nd Amendment. Which of the following was NOT part of the 44th Amendment?

options.option_text: Removed 'Right to Property' from Fundamental Rights; made it a legal right (Article 300-A)
Restored Lok Sabha/Assembly term to 5 years (from 6 under 42nd)
Safeguarded Articles 20 and 21 — now never suspendable even during Emergency

questions.explanation: FUNDAMENTAL DUTIES (Article 51-A, Part IV-A) were added by the 42nd AMENDMENT (1976), NOT the 44th. Originally 10 FDs; the 86th Amendment (2002) added an 11th (parents' duty to educate children 6-14). 44th Amendment (1978, Janata Party govt) REVERSALS: (1) Removed RIGHT TO PROPERTY (from Art 19(1)(f) + 31 → made it a legal right under Art 300-A, not a FR); (2) Restored LS/SLA term to 5 years; (3) ART 352 'armed rebellion' (replaced 'internal disturbance') + written Cabinet recommendation required for emergency; (4) ARTS 20 + 21 NEVER SUSPENDABLE even during emergency; (5) Restricted Ordinance-making; (6) Repealed judicial-review restrictions. Core 42nd provisions like Preamble changes + FDs SURVIVED the 44th.

questions.stem: The 52nd Amendment (1985) added the 10th Schedule dealing with:

options.option_text: Anti-defection law (disqualification on grounds of defection)
Scheduled tribal areas of NE India

questions.explanation: 52nd Amendment (1985, Rajiv Gandhi govt) added the TENTH SCHEDULE — ANTI-DEFECTION LAW. Disqualifies MPs/MLAs for: (1) Voluntarily giving up membership of their party; (2) Voting against party whip (or abstaining) on any motion. Originally allowed 'SPLIT' (if 1/3 defected together) — STRIKED DOWN by 91st Amendment (2003) which now requires 2/3 merger for exemption. Decision-making authority: Speaker (LS) / Chairman (RS) — their decision subject to judicial review per Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu (1993). 91st Amendment (2003) also limited CoM size to 15% of LS strength (min 12). The Anti-Defection Law was a response to 'Aaya Ram Gaya Ram' political culture (origin: Haryana 1967 — Gaya Lal changed parties 3 times in a fortnight).
